An object is an instance of a class.

6. How do you create an object in Java?
An object is generally created using the new keyword.
The new keyword creates memory for the object and returns its reference. That reference is stored in the reference variable d1.

20. Can a static method directly access instance variables?
No, a static method cannot directly access instance variables because static methods belong to the class, while instance variables belong to objects.
To access an instance variable inside a static method, we must create an object.
21. What are the commonly explained memory areas in Java?
For basic Java execution, memory is commonly explained using the following areas:
The exact memory organization may differ depending on the JVM implementation.
The method area stores class-level information.
The method area is shared among threads.
Heap memory is used to store objects and their instance data.
Whenever an object is created using the new keyword, memory is allocated in the heap.
The Dog object is created in heap memory.
Heap memory is shared among threads and is managed by the garbage collector.

25. What is the program counter register?
The program counter register stores the address of the instruction currently being executed by a thread.
Each thread has its own program counter register.
It helps the JVM keep track of the next instruction to execute.

28. What happens to memory when the program ends?
When the Java program finishes execution, the JVM terminates.
